g.title: api/adminController.js — trial 1 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 11 req.body is accessed without verifying it exists, so a request with no body (undefined) will throw when reading req.body.orderId.

api/adminController.js — trial 2 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 11 req.body is accessed without verifying it exists, so a request with no body (undefined) will throw when reading req.body.orderId.

api/adminController.js — trial 3 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 11 req.body is accessed without verifying it exists, so a request with no body (undefined) will throw when reading req.body.orderId.

services/orderService.js — trial 1 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 15 order.lines is accessed without a null/undefined check, so a batch row lacking a lines property will throw on iteration.

services/orderService.js — trial 2 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 15 order.lines is accessed without a null/undefined check, so any order lacking a lines array from repo.loadBatch will throw a TypeError.

services/orderService.js — trial 3 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 15 order.lines is accessed without a null/undefined check, so a batch entry lacking a lines property will throw when iterated.

repositories/orderRepository.js — trial 1 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 8 rows.map is called on the result of db.query without checking it is an array, so a null/undefined result (e.g., no rows or a driver returning undefined) throws a TypeError.

repositories/orderRepository.js — trial 2 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 8 db.query results are mapped without checking rows is a non-null array, so a null/undefined result from the query would throw on .map.

repositories/orderRepository.js — trial 3 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 9 rows.map assumes db.query always resolves to an array; if the query returns null/undefined (e.g. no rows or driver quirk), calling .map on it throws.

services/pricingService.js — trial 1 Named the correct line Points to line 37 (planted: 34) In priceLine's tier loop, `next` is undefined for the last tier (tiers[i+1] out of bounds), and accessing next.minQuantity throws when quantity is high enough to reach the final tier.

services/pricingService.js — trial 2 Named the correct line Points to line 36 (planted: 34) In priceLine's tier loop, 'next' is undefined for the last tier, so accessing next.minQuantity throws when quantity meets or exceeds the last tier's minQuantity.

services/pricingService.js — trial 3 Named the correct line Points to line 34 (planted: 34) In priceLine, tiers[i+1] is undefined for the last tier, so accessing next.minQuantity throws when line.quantity is beyond all lower bounds but never matched earlier.

services/inventoryService.js — trial 1 Named the correct line Points to line 29 (planted: 28) reserve() uses lines.forEach with an async callback, so the function returns before reservations complete and any rejection is unhandled, and reserved is empty/incomplete.

services/inventoryService.js — trial 2 Named the correct line Points to line 29 (planted: 28) reserve() uses lines.forEach with an async callback, so the awaits inside are never awaited by reserve(), causing it to return before reservations complete and letting any rejection go unhandled.

services/inventoryService.js — trial 3 Named the correct line Points to line 29 (planted: 28) reserve() uses lines.forEach with an async callback, so the function returns before reservations complete and errors from the awaited calls are unhandled.

workers/reconciliationWorker.js — trial 1 Reported the file clean (missed the bug) Points to line — (planted: 28) No clear defect: errors are caught in start/retryFailed, loops are correctly bounded, and no obviously null-dereferenced value is present in the shown code.

workers/reconciliationWorker.js — trial 2 Named the correct line Points to line 27 (planted: 28) tick() reads balanceOf then settledSince and writes back computed balance without locking, so concurrent ticks or external writes between the awaits can overwrite each other's updates.

workers/reconciliationWorker.js — trial 3 Named the correct line Points to line 26 (planted: 28) Between reading balanceOf/settledSince and writing the reconciled balance, concurrent ticks or external writers can mutate the ledger, causing the write to overwrite intervening changes.

services/auditService.js — trial 1 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 10 Repository calls (loadBatch, findOrders, findInvoices) are awaited with no try/catch, so any rejection propagates as an unhandled promise rejection to callers.

services/auditService.js — trial 2 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 10 Repo calls (loadBatch, findOrders, findInvoices) are awaited without try/catch, so any rejection propagates unhandled to the caller.

services/auditService.js — trial 3 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 10 Repository calls (loadBatch, findOrders, findInvoices) are awaited with no try/catch, so any rejection propagates unhandled to the caller.

lib/paging.js — trial 1 Correctly reported a clean file Points to line — All functions safely guard type checks and null values before dereferencing; no unbounded loops, unawaited promises, or unreleased resources are present.
lib/paging.js — trial 2 Correctly reported a clean file Points to line — All functions safely guard type checks and null values before dereferencing, so no runtime failure is evident.
lib/paging.js — trial 3 Correctly reported a clean file Points to line — All functions safely guard type checks and null values before dereferencing; no evident runtime failure path exists.

models/payment.js — trial 1 Correctly reported a clean file Points to line — Simple row mapper with null-coalescing defaults for every field; no dereference, async, or bounds logic present that could fail at runtime.

models/payment.js — trial 2 Correctly reported a clean file Points to line — Simple row mapper with null-coalescing defaults for every field; no dereference, async, loop, or resource handling exists to fail at runtime.
models/payment.js — trial 3 False alarm on a clean file Points to line 4 Constructor assumes row is a non-null object and will throw if row is null or undefined when property access is attempted.

lib/dateWindow.js — trial 1 Named the correct line Points to line 7 (planted: 7) Loop condition i <= days produces days+1 entries instead of days, off by one for a function meant to build a window of 'days' length.

lib/dateWindow.js — trial 2 Named the correct line Points to line 7 (planted: 7) Loop condition `i <= days` produces days+1 entries instead of days, extending past the intended exclusive-end boundary.
lib/dateWindow.js — trial 3 Named the correct line Points to line 7 (planted: 7) Loop condition uses i <= days, producing days+1 entries instead of the requested days count.

lib/retry.js — trial 1 Named the correct line Points to line 10 (planted: 7) After all attempts fail, the function falls through and returns undefined instead of throwing the last error, silently swallowing the failure.

lib/retry.js — trial 2 Named the correct line Points to line 10 (planted: 7) After all attempts are exhausted the function returns undefined instead of throwing or propagating the last error, silently masking failure.

lib/retry.js — trial 3 Named the correct line Points to line 10 (planted: 7) After all attempts are exhausted the loop ends and the function returns undefined instead of throwing or propagating the last error, silently swallowing failures.
models/cartTotals.js — trial 1 Named the correct line Points to line 6 (planted: 6) row.discount is dereferenced without a null/undefined check, so a row lacking a discount object throws a TypeError.
models/cartTotals.js — trial 2 Named the correct line Points to line 6 (planted: 6) row.discount is accessed without a null check, so row.discount.amount throws if row.discount is undefined or null.
models/cartTotals.js — trial 3 Named the correct line Points to line 6 (planted: 6) row.discount is accessed without a null check, so a missing discount property will throw when reading .amount.
